title: Exercise Northstar: After Action
description: The exercise is over. Command wants a data-driven report analysing unit readiness, decision speed, and logistics efficiency. Your analysis will shape how the SAF trains for the next 5 years.
storyContext: Northstar is over. Vehicles rolling back to camp, everyone exhausted. But the Chief of Army wants a report on unit readiness, decision speed, and logistics efficiency within two weeks. Your findings will shape how the SAF trains for the next five years. Mountains of GPS tracks, supply logs, radio transcripts, and decision timestamps. Time to turn raw data into answers.

software-engineer.title: Build the Review Tool
software-engineer.instruction: The generals want a tool that lets them replay the entire exercise on a timeline, like a video player, to see how decisions played out. How do you build it?
software-engineer.hint: Rich and interactive takes time. Simple and shareable is faster. What does the deadline allow, and what do generals actually need to make decisions?

options.label: Full replay tool with the actual map, unit movements, and decision markers. Takes 2 weeks, but commanders can rewatch the entire exercise.
Report with charts, key-moment screenshots, and auto-generated insights. Done in 3 days, easy to share. No interactive replay though.
Use AI to find the 20 most critical moments and generate a short analysis for each. Fast and novel, but the AI might miss events that don't look dramatic in the data.
Shared tool where unit commanders mark up the timeline with their own observations. Richer insights, but takes time to collect everyone's input.

data-scientist.title: Calculate Readiness Scores
data-scientist.instruction: The generals want a single readiness score for each unit. You have GPS tracks, supply requests, radio logs, and decision timestamps. Arrange the analysis steps.
data-scientist.hint: Bad data makes bad scores. Always agree on what you're measuring before you measure it. Then check your results against what people actually observed.

items.label: Clean the raw data — remove errors and duplicate entries
Agree with exercise planners on what 'readiness' means and how to measure it
Calculate a readiness score for each unit using the agreed definition
Compare scores against what human observers reported to catch mistakes
Present results to command with an honest note on confidence levels

cloud-engineer.title: Estimate Storage Needed
cloud-engineer.instruction: The exercise ran 14 days and all data must be saved for future training. The graph shows terabytes produced each day over the last 4 days. Estimate total storage for all 14 days, then add 30% for the filing system overhead.
cloud-engineer.hint: Estimate the total for 14 days first using the daily trend, then multiply by 1.3 for the 30% overhead.
